strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Price-led revenue growth: routine monthly price increases and route-level profitability discipline
posting_evidence: Senior Pricing Analyst (bilingual title), hybrid four days a week from Anjou (Montréal), Kitchener, Brampton, Ottawa or Calgary; $95,000–$120,000 base plus bonus; reposted about a month ago.
Mandate: recommend and implement monthly price increases in coordination with Sales and Billing, and assess and adjust pricing structures and outputs.
Builds and maintains pricing tools and infrastructure, and produces advanced customer and route profitability reports.
Internal pricing contact for Sales (not customers); guides less experienced pricing analysts and occasionally acts as team lead, with no formal supervisory duties.
Requires 5 years of relevant experience; waste-industry experience listed as both required and preferred; French/English bilingualism an asset.

news.summary: WM reported Q2 2026 revenue up 4.0%, driven by core price of 5.7% and collection-and-disposal yield of 3.6%, while collection-and-disposal volume fell 1.8% (0.4% excluding prior-year wildfire cleanup), partly from intentional exits from lower-margin residential business.

strategy_updates.interpretation: WM's growth is mostly pricing: core price of 5.7% against falling volume shows it is deliberately trading volume for margin, including exiting low-margin residential accounts. A Canadian analyst who sets monthly price increases and runs route-level profitability is the operating engine for that strategy (inference). The repost and multi-city location list suggest a hard-to-fill, network-wide Canadian role rather than a Quebec-specific one. For the candidate it is execution-heavy analytics with some team-lead exposure, not strategy ownership.
open_questions: How are monthly price increases targeted (CPI-indexed contracts, open-market accounts, fuel and environmental surcharges) and who approves them in Canada?
Does the role cover Quebec accounts specifically, and is French used day to day?
Is there a path from Senior Analyst to a pricing manager role, given the 'occasional team lead' wording?
strategy_updates.caveat: Built from a full Built In copy, not WM's own careers page. The Q2 figures are company-wide (mostly US) and were read from a search excerpt quoting the release because the release page blocked direct access.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Building a formal cement price architecture and pocket-margin discipline in Colombia
posting_evidence: Especialista de ingresos comerciales cemento, Bogotá (Teleport), permanent contract, professional level, salary confidential; published 2026-09-03 on elempleo.
Manages national pricing for the different business units against market conditions.
Defines and maintains price architecture by segment, product, region and channel; analyses competitive positioning and value-capture opportunities.
Monitors price, volume, mix and contribution; builds price waterfall and pocket-margin analyses and actionable insights for the sales force.
Only 1 year of experience required (pricing preferred); SAP SD, Power BI or Data Studio desirable; intermediate English desirable.
strategy_updates.interpretation: The mandate (price architecture by segment, region and channel, plus waterfall and pocket-margin analysis) is a standard price-realization toolkit. It suggests Holcim wants tighter control of discount leakage across its Colombian cement channels (inference). Context read today but older than three months: Holcim agreed in March 2026 to buy Cemex's Colombian building-materials operations for US$485 million, with closing expected at year-end. A larger plant and channel footprint would make a consistent national price architecture more urgent (inference; the posting does not mention it). The low experience requirement means this is an analytical support seat inside a larger commercial team, not the pricing decision-maker.
open_questions: Who owns final pricing decisions (the commercial director or a regional pricing lead), and where does this role sit relative to them?
Will the role extend to integrating pricing for the acquired Cemex assets once the deal closes?
How does Holcim handle competition-law constraints on cement pricing in Colombia, given past cartel sanctions in the sector?
strategy_updates.caveat: Based only on the elempleo posting; no Holcim careers page or recent (last three months) pricing news was found, and the link to the Cemex deal is inference.
